articles.title: Windows component store corruption
articles.summary: DISM and Windows Update failures can indicate corruption in the servicing component store.
articles.body: Confirm CBS or DISM evidence before using the approved servicing workflow. Preserve logs and complete prerequisites first.
articles.repairGuidance: Review and explicitly approve the WAID DISM repair workflow.

articles.title: Storage reliability warnings
articles.summary: SMART or Windows storage health warnings require cautious confirmation and data protection.
articles.body: A warning is not a vendor-independent failure prediction. Correlate health state, filesystem events, latency, and repeated crashes.

articles.title: DNS name-resolution failures
articles.summary: DNS failures can originate from resolver state, configuration, gateway, VPN, or upstream service.
articles.body: Confirm that basic network reachability works before considering a resolver reset. Do not infer internet failure from ICMP alone.
risks: VPN or managed policy may be affected
articles.repairGuidance: Review and explicitly approve the WAID DNS reset only after evidence confirms resolver-layer failure.

articles.title: Driver-related system crashes
articles.summary: Driver errors combined with minidump evidence can identify a suspected module without proving fault.
articles.body: Group repeated bug checks and compare the suspected module with signed-driver inventory and recent changes.
